newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes gain ground late with WTI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes gain ground late with WTI.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes gained further ground late Friday, on concerns that cold snap throughout the U.S. next week would raise benchmark West West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude.
NYMEX January crude settled up 75 cents at $24.47 a barrel, tracking a 3.04 cent a gallon rise in heating oil to 71.71 cents.
West Coast spot trade for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained quiet Friday, as traders exited early for the weekend.
Dealers said a flurry of trade could occur in California next week for producers of Canadian light crudes square inventories ahead of monthly pipeline shipping requests, slated for December 20.
Recent Line 63 deals were done on a posting plus basis only, traders said, with premiums talked $0.95 to $1.05 in the thinly traded market.
Line 63 at a discount to WTI had not been seen in months, traders said, noting deals done in the posting plus market fell between $0.95 abd $1.05.
Traders said higher inventories and a $0.50 to $1.00 decrease in posted prices forced heavy crudes lower mid-week.
Discounts for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said.
